claim.author: R0b-inference builder

basis.reason: y = min(y, c) + max(y − c, 0), and least squares is linear in y, so the two parts' coefficients add up to the primary's exactly; the build's test holds the sum.

claim.author: R0b-inference builder
claim.methods: refused when the logistic model's risk for any group of people runs to 0% or 100% (the arm and the covariates predict exactly whether they had the event): an arm, everyone (complete separation), or a group a linear program finds or cannot rule out; a partly separated fit is not read at its limit; the estimating equations run no such program, and are refused on a sign of separation in their independence start (no convergence, a coefficient past {coefficient_bound} on its column's own scale, or a fitted risk within {risk_floor} of 0 or 1), which can refuse a trial no one is separated in

coefficient_bound.unit: log odds per unit of a column, on its own scale

basis.reason: We refuse rather than report. At the fit's limit the standardized risks are finite (Lesaffre & Albert 1989, J R Stat Soc B 51:109), the separated people at their own outcome under every arm, but reading that fit was withdrawn in stage 1 (claims backtest B-281, its sixth review): ties to float rounding made it report a wrong risk difference, by up to 1.06 standard errors. Until a certificate robust to rounding exists, refusing is the honest fallback, with fewer covariates and describing the outcomes as its exits.

The refusal says the coefficients have no finite values, not that no finite estimate exists: the risk difference is finite at the limit (e.g. 0/50 against 20/50 is 0.40). Where an arm alone separates, Ye et al.'s variance, built from each arm's spread of outcomes around its fitted risks, is zero there, so no interval is given.

For a parallel trial, Newton's method runs on the raw columns first. When it does not converge, or converges with a sign of separation (a coefficient past the bound, a fitted risk within the floor), the separated people are found by one linear program (Albert & Anderson 1984, Biometrika 71:1; Konis 2007, as R's detectseparation does), solved by HiGHS on an orthonormal basis of the standardized columns; no one separated, the fit is redone on those columns. Where the program's answer is not decided to the module's tolerances, the effect is refused with the plain separation reason. The tolerances were measured on the stage-1 reviews' generators, not derived. The estimating equations run no program: the same signs in their independence start refuse them, and the Fires test on treated clusters that all had the event refuses there because Newton's method does not converge.

A coefficient past the bound, in log odds per unit of its column, is a sign of separation, not a proof of it, and is not scale-free: a covariate on a narrow scale passes it with no one separated, as a pH of 7.4 ± 0.02 with a log odds ratio of 60 per unit (about 1.2 per SD) does. A parallel trial then asks the linear program, which rules separation out, and reports the fit (the Silent test on such a pH, against statsmodels); with no bound the same fit is reported straight from Newton's method, so no test holds the bound itself. The estimating equations refuse on it (the scope part). The value is a convention, not tuned.

A fitted risk within the floor of 0 or 1 is read as a sign of separation. For a parallel trial it sends a converged fit to the linear program, and, no one separated, to the refit on standardized columns, whose information float64 must resolve: the Fires test spies on the program for a fit whose only extreme risk is one person's at an outlying dose, and the Silent test finds it not asked where no risk is near 0 or 1; the reported effect is statsmodels' either way. For the estimating equations the floor refuses in their independence start, as the bound does, and again at their own fit, a backstop no test reaches. The value is a float64 convention, not tuned.

The estimating equations' refusal runs no linear program, so it can refuse a cluster trial no one is separated in, and its reason then says, wrongly, that some group's risk runs to 0% or 100%. On 16 clusters with a pH of 7.4 ± 0.02 and a log odds ratio of 60 per unit, every one of 10 seeds was refused at the independence start's coefficient bound, where statsmodels' Logit and its exchangeable GEE give finite fits with fitted risks from 0.005 to 0.991 (the package's verifier, 2026-10-16). Giving the start the parallel trial's linear program, or a reason that is true, turns a refusal into a report or changes what the person reads, and is the orchestrator's to rule; until then the claim covers that case as a refusal whose stated cause can be wrong.

regime.words: a randomized trial with a yes/no outcome: the standardized risks of a logistic model with Ye et al.'s variance, or a cluster trial's estimating equations
